turns.text:
Well, it's certainly an unusual request! In my practice, I've encountered some interesting cases involving socks. One instance that comes to mind is a patient who had a significant phobia of socks. They would wear shoes with the socks removed or avoid wearing socks altogether. This fear, known as podophobia, is relatively uncommon but can have a significant impact on a person's daily life.

Another case involved a patient who used socks as a sort of comfort object. They would carry around multiple pairs of worn socks and would often sleep with them. This behavior is known as tactile stimming, a coping mechanism often associated with individuals on the autism spectrum. Understanding the reasons behind these behaviors can help us tailor our therapeutic approaches to better meet the needs of our patients.
